A 65-year-old female presents with a 1-month history of worsening fatigue and shortness of breath. On
physical examination, she appears generally pale. Laboratory results are as follows: | Hemoglobin | 5.8
g/dL | | --- | --- | | Hematocrit | 17% | | Mean corpuscular volume | 86 μm3 | | Leukocyte count |
6200/mm3 with a normal differential | | Platelet count | 240,000/mm3 | Bone marrow aspiration reveals
a complete absence of erythroid precursor cells. This patient’s condition is most likely associated with
which of the following? Answer Choices: (A) Parvovirus B19 infection (B) Cold agglutinins (C)
Myelodysplastic syndrome (D) FANCA mutation (E) Thymic tumor (F) Lead poisoning (G) Thymoma
with myasthenia gravis (H) Anti-erythropoietin antibodies (I) T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia
(J) Systemic lupus erythematosus
 A. T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia
B. Lead poisoning
C. Thymoma with myasthenia gravis
D. Parvovirus B19 infection
E. Myelodysplastic syndrome
F. Thymic tumor
G. Systemic lupus erythematosus
H. Anti-erythropoietin antibodies
I. Cold agglutinins
J. FANCA mutation
